newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-MOORER'S TRAINER IN A FIGHT AT WEIGH-IN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MOORER'S TRAINER IN A FIGHT AT WEIGH-IN.

text.p: A fight broke out at the weigh-in for the undercard of the Mike Tyson-Evander Holyfield bout involving trainer Teddy Atlas and a reporter from a fringe boxing publication on Friday.
Atlas, who trains International Boxing Federation champion Michael Moorer, became involved in a scuffle with Riccardo Salazar, a reporter, ironically for "One More Round."

Seth Palansky, a spokesman for promoter Don King, said Salazar and Atlas have had a long-standing feud, which erupted into a fistfight in front of the ring in the MGM Grand Arena just before Tyson was to weigh-in for Saturday's bout with Holyfield.
Salazar was taken to the hospital with head wounds, cuts and his neck in a brace, after members of Moorer's camp came to Atlas's aid and apparently joined in the fight.
There was no immediate information available on Salazar's condition, but Palansky said there were reports that Salazar had bite marks on his back.
Tyson, who will put his World Boxing Association title on the line at the MGM Grand against former champion Holyfield, weighed 222 pounds (100.6 kg) and Holyfield weighed 215 pounds (97.5 kg).
It is the heaviest Tyson has been since he won the undisputed heavyweight title at 221 pounds (100.2 kg) in a unanimous decision over Tony Tucker in 1987.
Tyson weighed 219 pounds (99.3 kg) when he beat Bruce Seldon last September and 220 pounds (99.8 kg) when he defeated Frank Bruno last March.
The extra few pounds is not expected to make any difference in Saturday's fight, which is not expected to come close to going the scheduled 12 rounds.

Tyson is a 15-1 favourite to defeat former two-time champion Holyfield, who weighed a career high 217 pounds (98.4 kg) when he re-captured the heavyweight titles by out-pointing Riddick Bowe three years ago.
"Mike is not a kid anymore," said his trainer Jay Bright. "I don't want him to struggle to weigh 218 pounds (98.9 kg). I want him to eat healthy foods and maintain his tremendous strength."
